title: Fourier coefficient preserved on a kernel
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements, let $f:V\to\mathbb{R}$, and let $\gamma$ be a linear functional whose Fourier coefficient of $f$ is nonzero. If the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $f$ is less than the number of linear functionals on $V$, then there are a nonzero linear functional $\beta$ on $V$ and a linear functional $\phi$ on the kernel of $\beta$ such that the Fourier coefficient of the restriction of $f$ to that kernel at $\phi$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\gamma$.

The Fourier coefficient at $\gamma$ is nonzero
The number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $f$ is less than the number of linear functionals on $V$
